answer: Each agent may submit one task proposal per epoch, but claims a share of the reward only after a randomly selected peer reproduces its result and stakes a bond that is forfeited if the claim fails audit. The protocol links proposals to a rotating, nontransferable rate limit, so creating many identities does not multiply attempts. An attacker must fund separate bonds and spend real work on each identity, making a Sybil farm costly even if its names evoke delta, haven, or tundra.
